In 480 BC the second Persian invasion of Greece happened, most people know it by the movie The 300, but the linchpin that saved Sparta and Athens and friends was the naval battle of Artemisium which happened at exactly the same time as the battle of Thermophyle (the movie 300).

The Persian fleet got caught in a storm on the way to Greece and lost about 1/3rd of their ships.

If that storm hadn't of happened, the Persian army would have over run more of the Greek city states (Corinth, Sparta) (Athens was sacked and the Greek lines fell back to the istmus of Corinth) and Greece never would have formed. Instead it would be a Persian nation. Rome never would have formed. The Persian orthodoxy would have spread east and established itself more permanently.

Democracy would never have been developed.

Without Rome the complete New Testament would not have been written. Christianity would not exist at all. Islam would not exist at all.

The complete modern idea of monotheism would ether not exist, or exist in a completely different form.

The whole western hemisphere would be totally different.

All because of one storm.
